formattedAddress: No. 2-1, Section 1, Jinan Rd, Dongmen Village, Zhongzheng District, Taipei City, Taiwan 100

text.text:
Su Hung is a Taiwanese restaurant with multiple Michelin stars, and you can definitely taste the quality in their dishes. Everything we tried was very flavorful and well executed.
That said, two dishes completely stole the show: the Taiwanese burger and the sweet and sour fish. Both were absolutely amazing, perfectly balanced, rich in flavor, and truly memorable. Honestly, I would come back just for those two.
A fantastic place for high-quality Taiwanese cuisine and definitely worth visiting.

text.text: A close friend, James Hsu took us to an incredible dinner at Su Hung Restaurant, which has been recognized as a Michelin Restaurant for three years. The quality and presentation of the food were impressive, and the flavors truly delighted us. However, the portion sizes were a bit smaller than what the price suggested, making it feel a bit pricey for the quality. This place is quite popular in Taipei, and securing a reservation can take several months. They offer two dining options: a casual setting on the ground floor and a more elegant fine dining experience upstairs. Keep in mind, there’s no free parking available, so finding a spot can be a bit challenging.

text.text: Its said they send their chef's back to Shanghai every year to learn and train more, so the menu is always changing and developing. They do every dish properly and right. It may not be "an abundance" of food, but every bite left me satisfied and content. Just make sure you have a reservation, because you might not otherwise be able to partake.

text.text: they have some good dishes, overall taste is okay,  but if you factor in prices, it's just average. This restaurant was Michelin guide listed, not to be confused with Michelin one star, but are charging Michelin 1 star inflated prices. The taste for the sweet and sour ribs is excellent, however the portion of the ribs were poor compare to what they charged.  I counted about a total of 10 pieces, because ribs are mostly just bone, You're not getting much meat. The steam buns were good, nothing to complain about, but not wow.  The Sichuan dish has good taste, but lacked peppercorn which is traditional and customary in authentic Sichuan cuisine, giving it the numbing spiciness but otherwise it's fine. Again good enough but lacks a wow factor. The Daikon pastry stuffing did not impress, it was too little, and too bland, it was wrapped mostly by flour dough. Customer service was also not up to not only the price they charge but the fact that they're Michelin guide listed. they simply lack training, and the understanding of customer orientation, some of the staff seem to not want to be there, but only are because they have to be there. The staff lacked knowledge of their own dishes, and when questions were asked, the answer was a I don't know, leaving the customer not knowing what to do with that, what or how to continue to order. None of the staff was new, which says they don't have excuses not knowing their own menu, which is the primary job of a wait staff.  My dining experience could have been better by more attentive and knowledgeable staff.

text.text: Delicious Shanghai style food!  Service was terrible!  There were three attendances, one male and two female ones.  The younger waitress was extremely attentive and diligent.  The other two were very lazy.
